A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and clearly describe the same GmNet research. However, both reference supplementary experiments and implementation details that are not included. v2 appends a NeurIPS checklist, not the referenced experimental appendix, limiting comparison of those materials.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 learning-curve experiments, ImageNet-1K classification and latency results, activation and GLU ablations, and convolution-kernel analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original GmNet experiments and reports revised ResNet diagnostics plus additional GLU experiments on MobileNetV2 and EfficientFormer-V2.

M1.justification: GmNet retains the same ReLU6-based gate, two 7×7 depth-wise convolutions, two 1×1 convolutions, and S1–S4 configurations. The architecture diagram is unchanged. The additional backbone experiments apply the existing GLU operation without introducing a new proposed component.

E1.justification: ImageNet-1K coverage is retained. v1 explicitly identifies CIFAR-10 for Section 3, whereas v2 leaves the dataset unnamed for its revised and additional frequency experiments. Consequently, their dataset coverage cannot be fully verified; adding backbones alone does not establish a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds MobileNetv4-Conv-S/M, LSNet-T/B, SwiftFormer-S, and UniRepLKNet-F, while removing EdgeViT-XS from that table despite retaining it in the expanded latency plot. The ResNet comparison replaces the ReLU variant with ReLU6. These update an otherwise largely retained comparator set.

E3.justification: The central ResNet diagnostic changes from four annular bands bounded by 6, 12, and 18 to binary low/high-frequency splits at thresholds 4, 7, and 10, and replaces ReLU with ReLU6. New MobileNetV2 and EfficientFormer-V2 probes use thresholds {6, 10} and {4, 8}, respectively. The ImageNet training recipe remains unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 4.1 and Figure 4 test whether inserting GLUs into MobileNetV2 and EfficientFormer-V2 improves frequency-specific and overall classification. This substantially extends the mechanism analysis beyond ResNet18. Figure 3 also replaces the earlier ResNet analysis, while the ImageNet activation, gate-design, and kernel-bandwidth analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three training runs for the frequency experiments and five testings in Tables 3 and 5. Neither provides defined error bars, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. v2's affirmative checklist answer adds no identifiable statistical procedure or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Replaced ResNet curves and new MobileNetV2/EfficientFormer-V2 curves substantially revise the reported frequency evidence; their changed settings preclude a direct v1-to-v2 performance comparison. Table 2 adds six baseline rows, removes EdgeViT-XS, and changes MobileOne-S2 GPU latency from 1.8 to 1.9 ms. GmNet accuracies remain 75.5%, 78.3%, 79.3%, and 81.5%, and Tables 3–5 retain their values.

T1.justification: Section 3 removes the explicit multi-band, Euclidean-distance mask definition and limits its formal setup to a binary high/low-frequency decomposition. That binary split already appeared in v1 Section 5.2, so it is not new theory. The two Fourier theorems, Lemma 3, and their mathematical reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: explaining gating through frequency analysis and proposing an efficient GmNet architecture that reduces low-frequency bias. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 connects the new backbone experiments to the importance of high-frequency learning for overall accuracy. Its new limitations paragraph states that larger models may already mitigate low-frequency bias and that simple GLU replacement may not help complex architectures. The earlier high-frequency robustness discussion is largely relocated.

D1.justification: v2 removes the CIFAR-10, CrossEntropyLoss, SGD learning-rate 0.1 description and the latency batch-size-one disclosure. It also replaces v1's public code URL with a checklist promise to release code upon acceptance. These materially reduce the supplied reproducibility and access information, although actual code withdrawal is not established and the ImageNet recipe remains.

R1.justification: References for MobileNetv4, LSNet, SwiftFormer, and UniRepLKNet are added; the EdgeViTs, PyTorch, and Frequency Principle references are removed. Most related-work prose and the positioning around gating, spectral bias, and lightweight networks remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses Section 3, combines its theoretical and experimental discussion, splits the method section into motivation and architecture, and moves discussion into a dedicated limitations section. It also expands introductory motivation and appends a checklist. Much of the abstract, related work, and ImageNet discussion remains verbatim.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two columns to a predominantly single-column layout with wrapped figures and tables. Figure 3 changes from sixteen panels to three, a new four-panel Figure 4 is added, Figure 1 is redrawn, and the latency plot is expanded. Existing architecture and bandwidth figures are relocated, and Table 2 is regrouped.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the mechanism evidence through experiments on two relevant lightweight architectures and adds useful applicability limits. However, it removes basic frequency-experiment settings, latency batch size, and the public code reference; the appended checklist does not supply the missing details. With stronger empirical support but reduced reproducibility information, the PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
